ai_summary:
Scottish wind generation is delivering an estimated 3.5 GW today, operating at 34.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity, while total GB wind output reaches 14.2 GW. This clean in-feed drives Scottish carbon intensity down to an exceptional 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the GB-wide average of 72 gCO2/kWh. However, structural transmission bottlenecks prevent this power from flowing south, forcing the curtailment of 8,644 MWh of Scottish generation so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids.

To replace this clean energy down-regulated behind constraints, fossil fuel plants elsewhere have burned an estimated 1,642,265 cubic meters of gas, releasing an avoidable 3,025 tonnes of CO2. Today’s curtailment actions have incurred constraint costs of about £488,490. If sustained, this daily run-rate projects an estimated total yearly cost of £178 million. Recovered through balancing mechanism charges across the wider system, this equates to a direct constraint premium of £57/MWh relative to the curtailed power, increasing typical UK consumer invoices by an estimated £0.60/MWh across total national electricity demand. Accelerating network reinforcement remains critical to eliminating these unnecessary carbon emissions and reducing system balancing costs for all British consumers.
